Before we begin

A few things
you might ask.
What should we bring to the first conversation?
+

One workflow and a person who knows it well. A few examples of where it slows down or goes wrong are more useful than a presentation. We will work out what else is needed together.

What if the workflow is not worth automating?
+

Then that is a useful result. We compare the likely value with the effort and risk before committing to a build. The next step may be a different workflow, a simpler change, or waiting.

Can you work within our security requirements?
+

Deployment, access, data flows and approval rules are part of the blueprint. Bring your security team into that discussion early. The Trust Center explains the available deployment approaches and documentation.

What happens after handover?
+

Your team operates the system with us alongside them for an agreed period. Further support or another workflow can be scoped separately. The code, prompts, evaluations and runbooks remain with you.

A few practical questions

Before we
get started.
Which practice systems can you connect?
+

We scope connections around the systems you use, including platforms such as athenahealth, eClinicalWorks, Epic, Dentrix and Open Dental. Availability depends on access, APIs and the workflow. We confirm those requirements before building.

Does the agent give medical advice?
+

No. These workflows cover administrative tasks such as scheduling, intake and billing questions. Clinical questions and urgent concerns follow the escalation rules agreed with your team.

How do you handle patient information?
+

Identity checks, access, retention and data flows are designed with your team. For covered workloads, review the applicable Business Associate Agreement and deployment scope before sharing patient information.

Can it work across multiple locations?
+

The workflow can use each location’s hours, providers, services and scheduling rules. We map the differences during discovery so the agent knows which location and team to involve.

What does the first build look like?
+

We start with one workflow, the systems it touches and a baseline to measure against. Your team tests realistic scenarios and handoffs before launch. Timing depends on the scope and access requirements.

03 / Data & access

Only the access
the work needs.

The boundaries belong in the build: credentials, approval rules, retention and a record of what happened.

01
Your data is not training data.

The commitment not to train on your data is contractual. Any required data egress is identified and approved before the build.

02
Credentials you can revoke.

Access is scoped to the actions a workflow needs. Your team issues the credentials and controls access to its systems.

03
A record your team can inspect.

Inputs, decisions, authorisation and outcomes are logged in your environment. Approval gates and recovery procedures are defined for the workflow.

04
Retention on your terms.

Retention follows the agreed policy. Deletion and written confirmation are available on request or at the end of the contract.
